U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.012%, Highest Intraday Level Since 2007, as Oil Surge Fuels Inflation Fears WSJ data showed the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.012% on Monday, its highest intraday level since 2007, as rising oil prices intensified inflation concerns and fueled a selloff in Treasurys. Brent crude briefly approached $110 a barrel amid heightened Middle East tensions. The Nasdaq fell about 1% in early trading as AI safety concerns weighed on technology stocks, while investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s rate decision on Wednesday. — link

Bitfinex Alpha: ETH ETF Inflows Outpace Bitcoin as Traders Use ETF Positions as Collateral for CME Futures Yield Strategies Bitfinex Alpha said traders are building positions in spot Ethereum ETFs to use as collateral for CME futures trades and generate yield, helping explain the stronger relative demand for ETH ETF products. Ethereum ETFs recorded $196.9 million in net inflows last week and $324.4 million so far in September, exceeding Bitcoin ETFs’ $307.3 million despite having only about one-sixth of their assets. Bitcoin ETFs posted $462.7 million in net outflows across all four trading days last week, reversing from a major source of institutional demand to a net seller. Bitfinex expects ETH to hold the September 11 daily low of $2,432 as support on pullbacks. — link

Ethereum L1 and Base Split on Account Abstraction Standards After EIP-8130 and EIP-8141 Collaboration Breaks Down Ethlabs researcher Derek Chiang said efforts to align EIP-8130 and EIP-8141 (Frame Transactions) broke down last week, leaving Ethereum L1 and Base to pursue different account abstraction standards. Both aim to support features such as gasless transactions and passkeys, but Ethereum L1 places greater emphasis on censorship resistance, privacy and security, while Base and other L2s prioritize scalability, configurability and compliance. Chiang said the divergence could fragment EVM transaction standards and wallet UX, though wallets and applications may ultimately abstract away the differences across chains. — link

Ethereum L1 Processes Record 203.9 Million Transactions in Q2 2026 as Average TPS Hits All-Time High of 25.9 Token Terminal reported that Ethereum L1 processed 203.9 million transactions in Q2 2026, up 68.4% year over year, while average throughput reached a record 25.9 TPS. The ETH staking rate rose to a record 32%, and the number of ETH-holding addresses reached 312.1 million, also an all-time high. Monthly active users fell 30% quarter over quarter to 9.2 million, while onchain fees increased 31.6% to $52.5 million and ETH burn revenue rose 112% to $17.1 million. Tokenized assets on Ethereum averaged about $203.1 billion in market value during the quarter, including roughly $176.8 billion in stablecoins and $20.8 billion in tokenized funds. — link
